query: The Tea Urn {The thesis lab runs on the tea urn, a dented copper monster that has outlived forty years of final-years. Round it, people confess things.|At the urn today someone is crying quietly into their mug about chapter three.|The urn. Someone has taped a list to it: STAGES OF THESIS GRIEF. Everyone has initialled the stage they're at.} {The urn is making the noise that means it's about to boil over.|Someone has hidden a tin of biscuits behind it, labelled NOT BISCUITS.|{season == "spring": The windows are open, and blossom keeps landing in the mugs.|The lamps are lit already, though it's barely evening.}} Stay and listen {You hear about an advisor who writes only in question marks, a source that turned out to be a forgery and a cat that ate a bibliography. You say almost nothing, and everyone thanks you.|You sit with the one crying about chapter three until they're laughing about chapter three.|You find your stage on the list and initial it. Then you listen to everyone else's, which is better than any advice.} Fill your mug and get back to work {You fill your mug and walk away from the confessions. Your carrel is quiet and your notes go well, and you feel slightly like a deserter.|You pat the crying student's shoulder on your way past and go back to work. It's the best you can do today.|You take your tea back to your carrel. Behind you, the list of stages grows another set of initials.}
